title: Observer and Adapter
summary: Let objects announce events without knowing who listens, and fit foreign interfaces into your own.

steps.title: Observer
body: An `Order` gets paid. Email must be sent, stock reserved, analytics updated. If `Order` calls all three, it is coupled to all three and every new reaction edits `Order`.
**Observer**: the subject announces "this happened"; any number of observers subscribe. In C# this is built in as **events**:
`Order` knows nothing about mail or stock. New reactions are new subscriptions.

steps.prompt: What is the main risk of the Observer pattern?
options: Flow becomes implicit: reading `MarkPaid` no longer tells you everything that happens
steps.explain: That is the trade-off. Use it when the subject truly should not know its listeners; for one fixed collaborator, a direct call is clearer.

steps.title: Adapter
body: You depend on `ILogger { void Log(string msg); }` (dependency inversion!). A third-party library offers `VendorLog.Write(int level, string text, DateTime at)`. Different shape, and you cannot edit it.
**Adapter**: a small class that implements *your* interface by translating calls to *theirs*.
public void Log(string msg) => vendor.Write(2, msg, DateTime.UtcNow);
The rest of your code keeps depending on `ILogger`. If you swap vendors, only the adapter changes. Adapters are how you keep foreign shapes at the edge.

steps.prompt: Match each scenario with the pattern.
pairs: A shopping cart should notify a badge, a total and analytics when it changes
Your code wants `IClock`, a library gives `NtpTime.Fetch()`
Pick a tax rule per country

steps.prompt: Complete the adapter so a vendor's `Shout(string)` fits your `INotifier.Notify(string)`.

steps.title: Adapt the thermometer
prompt: Your code uses `interface ITemperatureSensor { double Celsius(); }`. The hardware library gives you `LegacyThermo` (below, do not change it) which reports **tenths of a degree Fahrenheit** as an `int`.
Write `class ThermoAdapter(LegacyThermo legacy) : ITemperatureSensor` that converts: `F = raw / 10.0`, `C = (F - 32) * 5 / 9`, rounded to 1 decimal.

steps.title: Announce, don't call
prompt: `Stock` directly calls a `Reorderer` when it runs low, so it is coupled to it. Refactor to Observer:
- `Stock` gets `public event Action<string, int>? RanLow;` and raises it (item name, remaining count) when a `Take` leaves fewer than 3
- keep `Reorderer` and its `Orders` list; the tests subscribe it themselves: `stock.RanLow += reorderer.OnLow;`
starter: public void OnLow(string item, int left) => Orders.Add($"{item}:{left}");
solution: public void OnLow(string item, int left) => Orders.Add($"{item}:{left}");
template: Dojo.Eq("any listener can subscribe", new List<int> { 2, 1 }, dojoSeen);
